title: Madras High Court Seeks Replies on Plea to Probe CJP Spokesperson Saurav Das
excerpt: The Madras High Court on October 30 issued notice — returnable in six weeks — to the Centre, UIDAI, X and Instagram on a PIL seeking an inquiry into journalist Saurav Das's background and a block on his social media accounts. The allegations are unverified and the court has made no finding.
body:
• The Madras High Court on Friday issued notice on a public interest petition seeking an inquiry into the identity, nationality and background of journalist and Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das.
  • The plea also asks for Das's X and Instagram accounts to be blocked and for his passport and Aadhaar to be cancelled if the allegations are established.
  • Respondents — including the Home and External Affairs ministries, UIDAI, the Chennai passport office and the platforms' grievance officers — have six weeks to reply.
  • Issuing notice is a preliminary step that seeks responses; it is not a finding. The petition's claims are unverified, and Das has made no public response in the reports so far.

The Madras High Court on Friday (October 30) issued notice on a public interest litigation seeking a government inquiry into the identity, nationality and background of investigative journalist Saurav Das, spokesperson of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), and directions to block his social media accounts over allegedly derogatory remarks against the judiciary, according to Live Law and Bar and Bench.

What the petition asks

The petition (W.P. No. 44399 of 2026), filed by Ganesh Kumar of Kanchipuram district, identifies Das in its papers as "Yogesh Sharma alias Saurav Das" and asks the court to direct a detailed and fair probe into his background and personal details, including those of his parents. It seeks cancellation of his passport and Aadhaar card if the inquiry establishes he is not entitled to hold them. Separately, it asks the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology to block Das's accounts on X and Instagram and to restrain him from making further allegedly derogatory statements against the judiciary and judges of the Supreme Court. The petitioner's counsel, advocate B. Jagannath, told the court a representation dated October 7, 2026 had already been made to the authorities without action.

Who must respond

A division bench of Chief Justice S.A. Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan issued notice to the Regional Passport Officer in Chennai, the Chairperson of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), the Union Ministries of Home Affairs, External Affairs, and Law and Justice, the Secretary of MeitY, and the grievance officers of X and Instagram. The notice is returnable in six weeks, after which the matter will be heard again.

Allegations, not findings

None of the petition's claims — including questions it raises about Das's family origins — has been established by any judicial finding, and legal reporting on the case stresses that issuing notice does not amount to an endorsement of the allegations. Das is an investigative journalist and RTI activist who has become a prominent public face of the CJP, a youth-led movement that has organised protests over employment, examination irregularities and governance. No response from Das or the CJP appeared in the initial reports of Friday's hearing.

Why the case is being watched

The petition asks a court to set in motion identity verification by the passport and Aadhaar authorities and content blocking by the IT ministry in a single proceeding, aimed at a journalist who built his profile through RTI disclosures and criticism of institutions. Free-speech and press-freedom questions are likely to feature when the respondents — and Das — file their replies over the next six weeks.
